spatial_claims.claim: C is between A and B on line AB; D is beyond B on the ray AB with BD = AC. Collinear ordering: A, C, B, D.
AD is decomposed as AD = AB + BD, requiring D beyond B on the line.
AC + CB = AB, requiring C between A and B.
AB > AC since C is a proper interior point of AB (AC is a part of AB).

configuration_map: All points are collinear in the order A---C---B---D on a single straight line. Point C divides AB into segments AC (greater) and CB (lesser) in extreme and mean ratio. Point D is appended beyond B with BD = AC. Point B thus divides AD into segments AB and BD. This single collinear configuration is established in Step 1 and used consistently throughout all 13 steps. No auxiliary points off the line are constructed, no angles are formed, and no interior/exterior claims are made.
pass_reason: The proof operates entirely on a single collinear configuration A-C-B-D and uses purely algebraic manipulation of rectangle and square relationships among the segments. The collinear ordering is established once in Step 1 and every subsequent step is consistent with it. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, and no complex spatial configurations that could give rise to contradictions.
